samples.summary: Nested-table cell rectangle still copies an empty `text/plain` flavour — `getSelectedText` keeps the flat `layout.blocks.find` lookup the diff fixed everywhere else
samples.evidence: The change patched the two flat lookups it found (`normalizeRange` at selection.ts:128-130 and `getSelectedTableCells` at text-editor.ts:4331-4333) but `Selection.getSelectedText` still does `const lb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cr.blockId); if (!lb?.block.tableData) return '';` (selection.ts:761-762). A nested table is not in `layout.blocks`, so this returns `''`. Both `handleCopy` (text-editor.ts:1439) and `handleCut` (text-editor.ts:1482) write that as `text/plain` right next to the WAFFLEDOCS payload — so a cell rectangle inside a nested table copies nothing to any external application, and the cut path then calls `deleteSelection()` (text-editor.ts:1484), destroying the cells with only the internal flavour holding them. The new test only asserts the WAFFLEDOCS flavour (`nested-table-cell-range.test.ts`, 'copying a nested cell rectangle writes the cells'), so this half stays uncovered.

samples.summary: The new cycle guards are bypassed: `normalizeRange`'s own parent-chain walks (and `peer-cursor.ts`) still spin forever on the same cyclic `blockParentMap` the diff says would hang the tab
samples.evidence: The diff adds `seen` sets to `resolveNestedTableLayout` (table-layout.ts:488-494), `findOuterCellAddress` (text-editor.ts:3894-3906) and `findOutermostTableId` (text-editor.ts:3919-3925) on the stated ground that a looping parent chain is representable and would hang a render. But the very function the diff edits keeps two unguarded walks: `while (anchorTopId && layout.blocks.findIndex(...) === -1) { ... anchorTopId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }` (selection.ts:147-151) and the identical focus walk (selection.ts:153-157). With `a -> b -> a` neither id is ever in `layout.blocks`, so the loop never terminates — and this runs on every non-cell-range `normalizeRange`, i.e. every paint of an ordinary selection. `peer-cursor.ts:122-127` has the same unguarded `while (true)` walk on the render path. A tab hang is exactly the outcome the guard was added to prevent, so the protection is incomplete at the sites that need it most.

samples.summary: Shift+click inside a cell that contains a nested table now produces a whole-cell rectangle instead of extending the text selection
samples.evidence: Old shift+click compared only `anchorCellInfo.rowIndex/colIndex` with the top-level `cellAddr`, so a shift+click that landed inside a nested table *within the anchor's own cell* still took the text branch (`resolveOffsetInCell`) and extended the caret into the nested content. `resolveCellGesture` instead compares `resolvedCellInfo.tableBlockId` (the nested table) with `anchorTableId` (the outer table) at text-editor.ts:3956; they differ, so it falls through to the outer-table cell-range branch (3987-4001) and returns a `cells` target covering the anchor's whole cell. Shift+click from a paragraph in a cell into a nested table in that same cell therefore no longer extends the text selection. Defensible (it matches the drag path) but it is an unannounced behaviour change for the non-nested-anchor case.

samples.summary: `resolveCellGesture` calls `doc.getBlock()`, which throws on a stale id, from the uncaught mousedown path
samples.evidence: `this.doc.getBlock(anchorTableId)` (3965) and `this.doc.getBlock(resolveTableId)` (3989) throw `Block not found` (model/document.ts:239) when the layout's `blockParentMap` is stale relative to the document — the exact staleness the arrow-key path guards with a try/catch plus `invalidateLayout()` (text-editor.ts:3025-3032). The drag path already carried that risk, but routing shift+click through the same helper newly exposes `handleMouseDown` (2093-2094), which has no such catch, so a remote edit that removes the anchor's table between layout and click aborts the handler with an uncaught exception instead of falling back to the caret move. `this.doc.findBlock()` is the non-throwing variant and is what the sibling read at text-editor.ts:508 uses.

samples.summary: Clipboard copy of a cell rectangle now depends on a geometry resolver, so a layout-only failure silently degrades the copy
samples.evidence: `getSelectedTableCells` falls back to `resolveNestedTableLayout(cr.blockId, layout)?.dataBlock.tableData`. That resolver returns `undefined` for reasons unrelated to the data it is being asked for — no `layoutTable` (table-layout.ts:499), the containing cell being `merged` (533), or the nested-table line not being found in the cell's lines (558). In those cases `td` is undefined, `getSelectedTableCells` returns `null` (4334), and `handleCopy`/`handleCut` fall through to the block path (text-editor.ts:1443/1489) — writing the wrong payload, and in the cut case deleting the rectangle anyway via `deleteSelection()`, which resolves the same table through `doc.getBlock` and succeeds. A pure data lookup (`doc.findBlock(cr.blockId)?.tableData`, as `formatSourcePosition` at 508 already does) has none of these failure modes.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is present verbatim: selection.ts:761-762 resolves the cell-range table with the flat `layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cr.blockId)` and returns '' when it misses. The same change's own comments (selection.ts:120-130, text-editor.ts:4326-4333) establish that a nested table is absent from `layout.blocks`, and those two sites were converted to the `resolveNestedTableLayout` fallback while `getSelectedText` was not. The path is reachable: `getSelectedTableCells` (text-editor.ts:4331-4333) DOES resolve nested tables, so handleCopy enters the tableCells branch and writes the empty string as `text/plain` (text-editor.ts:1439); handleCut does the same at 1482 and then saveSnapshot/deleteSelection at 1483-1484, leaving the cut cells only in the internal WAFFLEDOCS flavour with nothing available to any external app. The new test (nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:219-237) asserts only the WAFFLEDOCS flavour, confirming the plain-text half is untested. No guard elsewhere prevents this; it is wrong behavior on a normal-use path, in the correctness lane.

finding.evidence: The diff adds `seen` sets to `resolveNestedTableLayout` (table-layout.ts:488-494), `findOuterCellAddress` (text-editor.ts:3894-3906) and `findOutermostTableId` (text-editor.ts:3919-3925) on the stated ground that a looping parent chain is representable and would hang a render. But the very function the diff edits keeps two unguarded walks: `while (anchorTopId && layout.blocks.findIndex(...) === -1) { ... anchorTopId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }` (selection.ts:147-151) and the identical focus walk (selection.ts:153-157). With `a -> b -> a` neither id is ever in `layout.blocks`, so the loop never terminates — and this runs on every non-cell-range `normalizeRange`, i.e. every paint of an ordinary selection. `peer-cursor.ts:122-127` has the same unguarded `while (true)` walk on the render path. verdict.reason: The finding checks out verbatim. The diff's own guards (table-layout.ts:487-495, text-editor.ts:3894-3906, 3919-3925) establish the premise that a looping blockParentMap chain is representable from peer-written CRDT ids and would hang the tab. Yet selection.ts:147-151 and 153-157 walk the same map with only two exit conditions — id found in layout.blocks, or no parentInfo — neither of which a 2-cycle of nested table ids ever satisfies (nested tables are by construction absent from layout.blocks, which is why the walk exists). peer-cursor.ts:122-127 is a bare `while (true)` with the same single `!parentInfo` break, and additionally unshifts into `nestingPath` each iteration, so it spins and grows memory. Both are on the render path: normalizeRange is invoked at selection.ts:562 (computeSelectionRects) and selection.ts:741, on the non-tableCellRange branch that handles ordinary selections; resolvePositionPixel is imported by selection.ts:7 for caret/peer painting. No upstream acyclicity validation exists — layout.ts:514-516 and table-layout.ts:428 merge/set parent entries unconditionally. No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, reachable, unguarded, and an infinite render-path loop is a correctness defect.
